a: SHA-256 is a widely used cryptographic hash for integrity checks.
Hashes are one-way; encryption is reversible with a key.
HMAC is a keyed hash used to authenticate messages.
Salts make each password hash unique even for identical passwords.
A pepper is a secret added to hashes and stored separately from the DB.
Use a slow password hash (Argon2/bcrypt/scrypt), not raw SHA-256.
Use constant-time compares for secrets to reduce timing leaks.
A nonce is a number used once to prevent replay in crypto protocols.
Initialization vectors must be unique per encryption under the same key.
Use TLS 1.2+; disable ancient SSL/TLS versions.
